correctness.rationale: The reduced vertex value h=c-b^2/(4a) has h'=P/(4a^2). Its fourth derivative is nonpositive on a>0, implying a three-root stationary bound and concavity of h''. That concavity excludes two minimum-type sign crossings. At a stationary vertex the Hessian Schur complement yields det Hessian=P'/(2a). Exact symbolic checks verify these identities and a rational example attains three feasible stationary roots with only the middle root minimum-capable.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 source derives the face quartic, allows up to four retained interior points, notes that some are saddles, and reports no concavity screening. It does not state the nonpositive fourth derivative, the three-root bound, uniqueness of the minimum-capable root, or the stationary Hessian-determinant formula. Searches of the recent source and related hexahedron-validation literature found no inspected prior coverage. Originality is only to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The theorem sharpens the exact candidate structure of a newly proposed hexahedral boundary-minimum algorithm: after quartic root isolation, at most one interior point per face needs minimum evaluation instead of up to four, with an exact simple-root curvature test and a correct multiple-root sign criterion.
